uncited: Adaptive Resolution Data Management encompasses techniques that partition volume data into regions or blocks assigned varying resolution levels to optimize storage and rendering costs.
It solves the problem of high memory bandwidth and processing demands for large-scale volumes by dynamically omitting low-detail regions and skipping empty spaces.

Unlike sibling methods such as [Mesh Simplification](1032-mesh-simplification.md) or [Wavelet-based Volume Rendering](1052-wavelet-based-volume-rendering.md) that maintain strict spatial locality or frequency-domain decomposition, this family often groups or assigns resolutions based on content metrics (e.g., variance, transfer function contribution, or rendering error), which enables significant data reduction but requires careful handling of interpolation and coordinate mapping.

Motion-aware Spatio-Temporal Sampling is a strategy that differentially processes regions based on gear levels, increasing temporal resolution for higher gears and splitting spatial samples for higher gears.

It sets itself apart by linearly interpolating temporal resolution between 1 and the total number of frames based on gear level, and splitting each sampled point into $2^{p(x,t)-1}$ points equally spaced within the ray segment.
Choose this method when rendering dynamic scenes with varying motion intensity to balance computational cost and reconstruction accuracy.
